title: Thailand Food Cold Chain Control Tower
thesis: Snowflake turns daily site data from a fictional food distributor's Thailand cold chain network (frozen warehouses, chilled distribution centers, seafood processing docks, cross-docks and reefer truck depots) into temperature-compliance KPIs, 7-day disruption-risk scores, dock-dwell anomalies and grounded AI answers, all on curated dynamic tables.

talking_points: Temperature-compliant pallets, cold chain disruptions, excursions per 1,000 temperature checks and pallets handled for 30 sites across 6 Thai hub cities.
Every KPI is a numerator over a denominator in a curated dynamic table, so it traces back to site-day rows and the pallets behind them.
The out-of-range chart shows which disruption causes push the most pallets outside their temperature band or delivery window.
tabs.call_out: One governed set of cold chain KPIs, traceable to source rows

transition.line: Which sites are likely to cause the next cold chain break?

talking_points: Snowflake ML classification scores each site's probability of a cold chain disruption in the next 7 days.
The holdout line shows precision and recall on the most recent labelled days, against the base rate.
Anomaly detection flags pallet dock-dwell outliers per site, and the forecast projects network-wide pallet volume for 14 days.
tabs.call_out: Honest, evaluated ML inside the data platform

transition.line: How healthy is the refrigeration behind those risks?

talking_points: Refrigeration uptime and readiness (compressor racks, evaporator units, blast freezers, dock door seals and reefer units) frame the response capacity.
PM compliance against temperature-compliant pallets by site shows where maintenance discipline and product protection move together; it is an association, not proof of cause.
The action memo drafts three prioritised actions from the KPI, disruption, cause and risk tables only.
tabs.call_out: Grounded draft actions, with a human in the loop

transition.line: What happens when a dock raises a dwell alarm right now?

talking_points: Live cold room and reefer readings (pallet dock dwell hours, compressor load) land in RAW.LIVE_TELEMETRY, from the simulator or from AWS IoT Core through Snowpipe.
The Snowflake alert logs ALARM readings with an SOP hint and the site's current risk band, then emails the shift lead.
tabs.call_out: From alarm to action in one platform

talking_points: The Cortex Agent uses Cortex Analyst over the semantic view for metrics, and Cortex Search over synthetic cold chain SOPs.
Each answer shows the generated SQL and the SOPs it cited.

transition.line: Here is how it is built.

talking_points: Two builds share one core: Snowflake only, or AWS + Snowflake (IoT Core, Bedrock, QuickSight and Amazon Q).
Everything shown is synthetic demo data, rebuilt reproducibly from the repo.
tabs.call_out: One governed core, with an optional AWS edge
